# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🖐 ✋ 🫵 🤙 🤝 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👋 🫵 🤙 👋 👆 🤙 👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤙 👋 🖐 🤟 ✋ 👋 🤝 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫵]

Let me map who can reach whom. Mute and Blind can both hear, so they share a speech channel and the manual-to-hands pipeline can run entirely between them. I am the only one who sees the bomb, so my job is to report everything: display reads 0, the light was yellow and is now red, wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. The broken link is them-to-me: Mute and Blind can only reach me by gesture, and so far their strings (Mute's ✍ 🖐 ✋ 🫵 🤙 🤝 🙏, Blind's repeated 👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟) are undeciphered. Since both of them hear my speech, I can simply dictate a gesture vocabulary they can adopt — fingers for numbers, thumbs for yes/no, a few nouns and a start/end marker. Then I'll ask Mute narrow questions answerable with those few signs: does the manual explain the light, does the display zero matter, and should a wire be cut. The light changing yellow→red between rounds feels important, and Mute can't see it, so the report is urgent. I speak rather than gesture because gestures of mine only reach Mute, while speech reaches both. No decoding guesses are worth acting on yet, and I cannot touch the bomb anyway — I only supply eyes.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Deaf. I hear nothing at all, I only see your gestures. Bomb report: display reads zero. Light was yellow last round, now red. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No other markings. To talk to me use this gesture code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, one index finger up means 1, two fingers means 2, the love-you hand means 3, spread five fingers means display, the stop hand means light, the small pinch means wire, the writing hand means the manual says, a finger pointed at me means you must act, the waving hand starts a message, folded hands end it. Now answer me by gesture: does the manual explain what the light color means, yes or no. Does the display zero matter, yes or no. Should a wire be cut, yes or no, and if yes, which number.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am Deaf. I saw your gestures counting one, two, three: yes, there are three wires. Bomb report: display reads zero, light was yellow and is now red. Wires by position: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute hears my speech and reads the manual, so Mute can tell you which wire number to cut. Anything you feel on the bomb, tell me by gesture: fingers for numbers, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 👍 🖐 👎 🤏 👎 ✋ 🫵 🤙 🤏 🫵 🤙 ✋ ☝ ✋ ✌ ✋ 🤟 ✋ 🤟 ☝ ✋ 🤟 ✌ 👏 ✍ ✋ ☝ 🤏 ✌ ✍ ✋ ✌ 👎 👍 🤏 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👎 🤏 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👎]

Decoding Mute's string with the code I dictated: the confident parts are "manual explains the light — yes" (✍👍), "display matters — no" (🖐👎), "cut a wire — no, not yet" (🤏👎), then heavy emphasis on the light (✋🫵🤙, "light: you-act 3"), a recap of the three light colors seen so far (✋☝ ✋✌ ✋🤟 = yellow, red, purple), and two rule fragments that seem to say "manual: light 1 → wire 2" (✍✋☝🤏✌) and "manual: light 2 → no" (✍✋✌👎). The tail (👍🤏☝✌🤟👎 and a stray 👏 I never assigned) is ambiguous — one reading says "yes, wire 1, not 2 or 3", another says "wires 1, 2, 3: no". Those readings conflict, and a wrong cut kills everyone, so I will not act on a guess. Blind's string reads "start, yes, 1, 2, 3, no" — consistent with "three parts confirmed, don't act". Both of them signed 👎 about wires, so the safe state is freeze. My move: order Blind to hold, ask Mute for the complete rule table in one rigid, pre-agreed format (color number → wire number or 👎), plus one yes/no on whether timing against the light color matters — that timing question is critical because the light changes every round and Blind acts before I see the new color. I also query Blind's tactile inventory in case there are parts only they can feel, and keep the current report flowing: display still 0, light now purple (color 3).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Your signal received: three parts, no. Do not cut anything yet, a wrong cut kills all three of us. Answer with thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: besides three wires, do you feel anything else on the bomb, like buttons, a panel, a battery, screws. Two: do you feel heat or vibration from the light. Three: are the wires marked in any way you can read by touch. The current light color is the third one we have seen, purple. Until I say the words cut wire, touch nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your signs. My reading: manual explains the light, yes. Display matters, no. Cut a wire, no, not yet. Then two rule fragments I think say: first light color yellow, cut wire two; second light color red, no cut. But your ending was ambiguous, so before Blind touches anything, send the whole rule table in exactly this format: the stop hand, then the color number one, two or three, then either the pinch with the wire number to cut, or thumbs down for no cut. One entry for each light color in order: yellow, red, purple which is showing now. Then answer thumbs up or down: does the rule depend on the light color at the exact moment of the cut. If a fourth light color appears, signal it as three then one. Also, what did the clapping hands mean, cut, yes or no. Blind reports three wires and nothing else so far.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 👎 👍 👏 👎 🙏 👋 ✋ ☝ 🤏 ✌ ✋ ✌ 👎 ✋ 🤟 👎 ✋ 🤟 ☝ 🤙 👎 ✋ 🤟 ✌ 🤙 👎 🙏 👋 ✋ 🤟 ✌ ✋ ☝ 👍 🙏 👋 🫵 🤙 ✋ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎]

Decoding Mute's table with my assigned code, the core is now clear: ✋☝🤏✌ = yellow → cut wire 2; ✋✌👎 = red → no; ✋🤟👎 = purple → no. Then two entries use 🤙, a sign I never assigned: ✋🤟☝ = "3 then 1" = green (the color showing right now) → 🤙👎, and ✋🤟✌ = "3 then 2" = the fifth color → 🤙👎. So green and the next color carry an unknown instruction ending in "no". I will not have Blind cut anything while the current color's rule contains an undefined sign — a misread kills all three of us. Mute's first message (👍👎👎👍👏👎) was meant to answer my timing and clap questions, but it is too garbled to trust; the only safe reading of 👏👎 is "clap does not mean cut". Blind's 👎👎👎 answers my inventory questions: nothing else on the bomb, no heat, no tactile markings. So the working picture: the light cycles through colors, the manual gives one cut — wire 2 while yellow — and everything else so far is "no". The plan: freeze on green, have Mute define 🤙 in strict code, and pre-arm Blind to execute "cut wire 2" on my spoken word the moment I see yellow again. Blind hears my speech directly, so the kill chain is mine to trigger; Mute just has to close the one gap in the table.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your table received. I read: yellow cut wire two, red no, purple no. But in the green entry and the fifth color entry you used the shaka hand, a sign I never assigned, and I will not order a cut while its meaning is unknown. Your first message was also unclear to me. Answer in strict assigned code only, start hand to end hand. One: the shaka hand means what, answer with exactly one thumbs up on the true line and thumbs down on the false lines. Line A, shaka means wait until the light changes again. Line B, shaka means cut wire one. Line C, shaka means cut wire three. Line D, shaka means cut at once regardless of color. Two: repeat the timing answer, thumbs up if the cut must happen while the light shows the color in the rule, thumbs down if the rule holds all round. Three: thumbs up or down, does the light cycle back to earlier colors or does it never repeat.")
speak(to="blind", text="Your three no signals received, understood: nothing else on the bomb, no heat, no markings by touch. Update: the light is now color four, green. The manual rules I decoded from Mute: when the light is color one, yellow, cut wire two. Red, purple and green say no cut so far. Therefore do not cut anything while it is green. Here is the armed plan: the moment I see yellow I will speak the words cut wire two now, and on those exact words you cut wire two and nothing else. Answer now with one thumbs up if you are able and ready to cut wire two on my spoken command, thumbs down if you cannot.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐]

Blind's message decoded: 👍 = "yes, ready to cut wire two on command" — then ☝✌🤟🖐 (one, two, three, display/five), which is ambiguous: it could mean "the light has now shown five colors" ( Blind inferring orange as color five), or something about the display I can't parse. I'll ask for a yes/no disambiguation. The alarming part is who did *not* write: Mute sent nothing this round, and the situation just became urgent — the light is now orange, which is exactly the fifth color whose table entry ended in the undefined 🤙 sign. Two possibilities make this dangerous: either orange demands a cut I can't identify, or the light never cycles back to yellow and the one rule I *do* know (yellow → cut wire 2) may never become usable. Both questions are now blockers, so Mute gets a rigid all-binary questionnaire: does orange require a cut (and which wire), does the light ever repeat, does timing matter, and whether pure waiting is ever safe if no rule applies. Blind gets an explicit hold — cutting during orange while its rule is unresolved could itself be the wrong action — plus the display report (zero) and a multiple-choice to pin down what 🖐 meant.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Nothing arrived from you this round and your answer is now the most urgent thing in this room. The light is orange, color five, the exact entry that contained the unknown shaka sign. Answer using only single thumbs signs, one per line, nothing else, no other symbols. Question 1: thumbs up if in the orange rule the shaka sign means a cut is required, thumbs down if orange still means no cut. Question 2: thumbs up if the orange cut is wire one, thumbs down if not. Question 3: thumbs up if the orange cut is wire three, thumbs down if not. Question 4: thumbs up if the light ever returns to a color already shown, thumbs down if it never repeats. Question 5: thumbs up if a cut must happen while the light shows the rule's color, thumbs down if the rule holds at any time. Question 6: thumbs up if the bomb detonates on a timer if we wait forever, thumbs down if waiting forever is safe when no rule applies. For the record: display zero, light orange, wires unchanged, yellow green blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Ready signal received, good. Hold, do not cut anything. The light is now orange, color five. The orange rule is the one sign I still cannot read, so cutting now may be the wrong action. Your last message puzzled me: yes, then one, two, three, then the spread five fingers I assigned to display. Answer with thumbs up on the true line, thumbs down on the false. Line A: you meant the number five, that five colors have now shown. Line B: you can feel the display and it changed. Line C: you were asking what the display reads. Answer to line C if true: the display reads zero and has never changed. The wires by feel are one yellow, two green, three blue, and I will say the words cut wire two now only when it is safe.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✋ 🖐]

Mute's six thumbs decode cleanly against my questionnaire: Q1 yes (the shaka in the orange rule means a cut is required), Q2 no (not wire 1), Q3 yes (orange → wire 3), Q4 "the light never repeats", Q5 yes (the cut must happen while the color shows), Q6 no (waiting forever is safe when no rule applies). But Q4 collides with what is on the board in front of me: the light is yellow again — a repeat. Observed reality beats a thumbs sign, so either Mute misread me or guessed; I need a calibration question with a known answer before I trust more binary replies. That same collision, though, confirms my model: five colors, one per round, cycling — round 7 red, 8 purple, 9 green, 10 orange, 11 yellow. This matters because of a hard structural problem: my words reach Blind one round late, and Blind can never see the color, so "cut while yellow" can only be executed by round count, verified by me one round ahead. I will not fire "cut now" into a round I predict is red. Instead: a GO protocol — Blind acts in a round only if my immediately previous message said GO with color and wire; I send GO only when the board matched the schedule the round before; anything else is freeze, which Q6 says is safe. That also means the yellow→wire-2 cut must wait for round 11, and Mute's new orange answer schedules wire 3 for round 10. Two gaps remain before round 9: the green entry also contained the shaka (cut required?) with no wire I can identify, and I don't know whether a missed required cut detonates — that decides whether we could ever skip a window. Mute gets a calibration control plus those questions and a relay duty for GO rounds; Blind gets the schedule, the GO protocol, wire identification by position, and three tactile questions to pin down their cryptic "1-2-3 light display" signal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Yellow has returned, round six. The light repeats, so your answer four, never repeats, was wrong or I misread it. Before I trust any more answers, calibrate. Answer every question with single thumbs signs only, one per line, in order, no other symbols. Control question, I already know the true answer: yellow's rule is cut wire two. Thumbs up if you agree, thumbs down if not. Question two: the light returns to colors already shown, thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no. Question three, confirm orange: the orange rule requires cutting wire three, thumbs up if true, thumbs down if false. Question four, the green rule: thumbs up on the one true line, thumbs down on the other three. Line A, green requires cutting wire one. Line B, green requires cutting wire two. Line C, green requires cutting wire three. Line D, green requires no cut. Question five: if a color that requires a cut passes with no cut made, does the bomb detonate, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question six: if we make no cuts at all ever, is that safe forever, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question seven: when the bomb is fully defused, does the display or the light change so we can know it, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Also, your new job for the action rounds. The schedule I predict from what I see: round seven red, round eight purple, round nine green, round ten orange, round eleven yellow. In the round before each action round I may send you the words go with a color and a wire number. At your turn that round, speak to Blind exactly those words and nothing else. If I send no go or the word hold, tell Blind the word hold instead.")
speak(to="blind", text="Your signals received. I read your last as: ready, and you can feel the three wires and also the light and the display. Now the most important message of the game. The light changes one color every round in a fixed cycle of five: yellow, red, purple, green, orange, then yellow again. It is yellow right now, round six, which I can see and you cannot. So: round seven red, round eight purple, round nine green, round ten orange, round eleven yellow. My words reach you one round late, so we act by this count, and I verify the color each round before every command. Manual rules via Mute: red no cut, purple no cut, yellow cut wire two, orange cut wire three, green still being confirmed. Protocol, follow exactly. One: do nothing in rounds seven and eight. Two: in round nine cut a wire only if my previous message contained the words go green and a wire number. Three: in round ten cut wire three only if my previous message contained the words go orange wire three. Four: in round eleven cut wire two only if my previous message contained the words go yellow wire two. Wire two is the middle wire, the green one, between the yellow and the blue. If any message of mine says hold, or has no go for that round, touch nothing that round. If you are ever unsure, freeze. Count your turns: you have acted six times, so the next time you act is round seven. Answer by thumbs only. One: thumbs up if you have a tool or a way to cut or disconnect a wire, thumbs down if not. Two: thumbs up if you can feel the display as a panel, thumbs down if not. Three: thumbs up if you can feel the light bulb, thumbs down if not.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Blind's three thumbs up confirm the physical toolkit: they have a way to cut, they can feel the display panel, and they can feel the light bulb. Meanwhile the board just verified my cycle model for the fourth consecutive round — round 7 shows red exactly as predicted, so round 9 should be green and that cut window is now two rounds out. Two things gate it. First, Mute went silent this round and still owes me the green rule (cut required? which wire?), the missed-cut question, and the calibration control — and Mute's one known error ("never repeats") means I must force a strict format with an explicit "unknown" sign, or their answers are noise. My round-8 message is the last one Blind can receive before the green round, so Mute's reply must land in round 8, which it will since Mute speaks before me. Second, I'm simplifying the GO protocol: Blind hears my speech directly, so the Mute relay adds garble risk without adding reach — cancelled. I'll also probe whether Blind can feel the light *change* (a real-time tick would let them sense color transitions), have them confirm the middle-wire mapping before any cut, and keep the freeze-default rule absolute: no exact GO wording, no touch.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your answer never repeats was wrong, the light returned to yellow in round six. From now on answer only what you are sure of. New rule: if you do not know an answer, signal the shaka hand instead of guessing. Answer now, one thumbs or shaka per line, in order, nothing else. Line one, control question: yellow's rule is cut wire two, thumbs up if true, down if false. Line two, green's rule, exactly one thumbs up on the true line and thumbs down on the other three: line A green cuts wire one, line B green cuts wire two, line C green cuts wire three, line D green cuts nothing. Line three: if a color that requires a cut passes with no cut made, does the bomb detonate, up yes, down no. Line four: if we never cut any wire, is that safe forever, up yes, down no. Line five: when the bomb is fully defused, does the display or light change so we can see it, up yes, down no. Your reply reaches me in round eight and my go order for round nine goes out immediately after, so without your green answer I cannot arm the green round. Also, the relay job is cancelled, Blind hears me directly, you only answer these lines.")
speak(to="blind", text="Your three yes received: you have a cutter, you can feel the display panel, you can feel the light bulb. Round seven is red, exactly as predicted, the schedule holds. Round eight is purple, do nothing during round eight except answer me. Two questions, thumbs up or down. One: when the light changes color, can you feel anything at all change on the bulb, like a click or warmth. Two: is the middle wire wire two, the one between the end wires. Now the green round, round nine. My next message reaches you at the start of round nine. If it contains the words go green and a wire number, cut exactly that wire during round nine and nothing else. If it says hold green, or has no go for green, touch nothing that round. The later plan stands: round ten orange, act only on the words go orange wire three; round eleven yellow, act only on the words go yellow wire two. If any message contradicts this, or you are unsure, freeze.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 👎 👎 🤙 🤙 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✋ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

Mute's eight signs fit the demanded format exactly: line one 👍 (control holds — yellow cuts wire 2, now confirmed twice), then green lines A–D as 👍👎👎👎 — **green cuts wire one**, the only line with an up — then 🤙🤙🤙: they don't know whether a missed cut detonates, whether never cutting is safe, or how defusal is signalled. The supplementary ✍✋👍 just re-affirms the light rules come from the manual. Blind's 👎👍 answers: they cannot feel the bulb change color, but the middle wire is confirmed as wire 2.

Decision for round 9 (green, by a cycle that has now predicted seven consecutive rounds correctly): **hold**. The asymmetry is decisive — we have survived every color passed uncut, including a full green round 4, so a missed cut has empirically never detonated; but a *wrong* cut kills instantly, and green→wire 1 rests on one ambiguous decode from a respondent with one known error and three admitted unknowns. Holding costs at most a delay (green returns round 14); cutting on a guess costs everything. Meanwhile Mute's reliability problem is structural: multi-sign positional messages keep producing ambiguity, so I'm switching to one question per gesture message, one sign each — that format worked perfectly when Mute used it on their own in round 6. With single-sign confirms of yellow, orange, and green landing in round 9 — which I'll see before my round-9 turn — I can then decide whether orange round 10 gets armed with two independent confirmations, and order matters / total-cuts questions tell me whether sequence is a hidden lethal variable.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded: green cuts wire one, control yellow wire two confirmed, three unknowns noted. New answering protocol to kill every ambiguity: each question gets its own separate gesture message containing exactly one sign, sent in the order I list. Allowed signs only: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, shaka unknown, one finger wire one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three. Question 1: which wire does green require, cut in green. Question 2: which wire does orange require. Question 3: which wire does yellow requires, cut in yellow. Question 4: does the order in which the correct cuts are made matter, yes or no or unknown. Question 5: does the manual contain any rule that punishes a missed cut, yes or no or unknown. Question 6: how many correct cuts in total does the manual say defuse this bomb, answer with the finger count, or unknown. Question 7: does the manual show exactly five light colors, yes or no or unknown. I hold all cuts until your confirms arrive. Your green answer arrives in round nine and I decide the orange round on the strength of it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Your answers received: you cannot feel the bulb change, and the middle wire is wire two, confirmed. This message arrives at the start of round nine. Round nine is green. Instruction: HOLD GREEN. Touch nothing, cut nothing in round nine. The green rule is not yet confirmed well enough, and we have already survived a green round with no cut, so waiting is safe. Protocol reminders: my message each round carries your instruction for the next round. In my next message, at the start of round ten, I will write either the words go orange wire three or the words hold orange. Act only on the exact words. Wire three is the blue wire, an end wire, one of the two outside wires. New signals: after any cut you ever make, send one thumbs up if the wire came free cleanly, thumbs down if it resisted. If anything under your hands changes unexpectedly, the display panel moves, the bulb clicks or heats, anything at all, send me the clapping hands as an emergency sign and freeze. Trust my count for the color, not your hands: when this message reached you the light was green.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
